jobs.title: Senior R&D Technician, Space PV Prototyping
jobs.description:
At Tandem PV, we are a team of people who are passionate about building a more sustainable world by bringing cost effective solar panels onto the market. We’re scaling metal-halide perovskite solar technology to make best-in-class mechanically stacked tandem modules. We have built efficient, durable cells, monolithic multi-cell submodules, and packaged modules with our scalable, low-cost process. Our next focus is expanding our team to work in our new pilot manufacturing facility.

**Job Summary:**

As a Senior R&D Technician, Space PV Prototyping, you will work with our engineers and technicians to build prototype solar devices for spacecraft on ultrathin and flexible substrates: preparing substrates, running deposition, coating and patterning tools, laminating covers, and measuring results. Much of what you handle is a fraction of a millimeter thick and hard to replace, so careful execution, exact adherence to written procedures and meticulous records are central to the role. Your work produces the consistent, well-documented sample sets that our development and test campaigns depend on.

**To be great at this role, you will have:**

* Clean, inspect, photograph and log substrates, and keep accurate inventory of limited, high-value materials.
* Load and run sputter and evaporation processes, including bake-outs and controlled pump-down and vent sequences.
* Coat and thermally process device layers to fixed recipes, and flag anything that looks different from previous runs.
* Set up and run laser patterning steps, then inspect the result under a microscope and measure electrical isolation.
* Laminate cover materials, including very thin ones, and inspect for voids and edge-seal quality; handle ultrathin substrates and release them from carriers once formally qualified.
* Perform routine metrology: sheet-resistance mapping, transmittance, profilometry, optical microscopy, luminescence imaging and current-voltage measurement.
* Keep run logs and per-part travelers (tools, recipes, temperatures, vacuum cycles, operator, timestamps), and prepare and ship sample batches to external test partners.
* Build, label, mount and wire coupon sets for test campaigns and exposure chambers, and perform routine tool care, including early warning when a tool starts to drift.

**Qualifications:**

* Steady hands and patience for delicate manual work; this is the single most important qualification for the role.
* Meticulous documentation habits: detailed, legible and consistent notes of processing conditions.
* Follows written procedures exactly, and speaks up when a procedure does not match what is actually in front of you.
* Problem-solving orientation and the ability to work autonomously once trained, as part of a team in a scientific or technical environment.
* Adaptability across a wide range of laboratory tasks and willingness to learn new concepts, tools and measurements.
* Comfortable with basic laboratory arithmetic, unit conversion, and reading a specification or drawing.
* Ability to perform the essential functions of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation, including working in a cleanroom environment while wearing required PPE and gowning; working on your feet for extended periods as required by laboratory activities; occasionally lifting, carrying, or moving materials weighing up to approximately 25 pounds; and safely working in laboratory and manufacturing environments where solvents, chemicals, and Class 4 laser systems may be present. Employees will be required to follow applicable safety procedures and complete required safety training.

**Preferred Experience:**

* Laboratory, cleanroom, semiconductor, display or precision manufacturing background, including handling thin glass, silicon wafers or display panels.
* Operation of vacuum systems, thermal evaporation or sputter deposition, solution coating (blade or slot-die), or laser tools.
* Experience in an ISO 9001, AS9100 or similarly controlled environment, or with fine assembly, soldering, precision dispensing or hermetic sealing.

This position may require access to technology and/or technical data subject to U.S. export-control laws. Any eligibility or access requirements will be applied in accordance with applicable U.S. export-control laws, regulations, licenses or authorizations, government-contract requirements, and applicable anti-discrimination laws.

Tandem PV uses perovskite & silicon mechanically-stacked tandems to upgrade silicon solar panels, sharply decreasing installed systems costs, significantly increasing module manufacturing profit margins, and opening up vast new solar markets in the US and worldwide. TPV was co-founded by Stanford PhDs Colin Bailie and Chris Eberspacher; is advised by industry experts from Corning, First Solar, Vivint Solar, and Kateeva; has raised more than $50M in Series A funding. We were recently recognized as the Best Pre-Commercial Venture of 2025 by the Industry Growth Forum (IGF)

We are a team of people who are passionate about building a more sustainable world by delivering a new generation of solar panels to the market. We are constantly growing and are always looking for dedicated, hardworking, and empathetic teammates.

Tandem PV is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply.

jobs.title: Research Lab Technician II
jobs.description:
**Job ID** REQ20181555 **Category** Laboratory

  

USC Norris Comprehensive Cancer Center is seeking a Research Lab Technician II to join the Preclinical Models Shared Resource (PMSR) core facility. The Research Lab Technician II will support the day-to-day operations of PMSR, a shared core facility within the USC Norris Comprehensive Cancer Center that provides preclinical oncology research services to investigators across USC. PMSR supports multiple investigator-initiated projects through the delivery of high-quality preclinical research services.

The position will conduct and assist with in vivo preclinical studies using mouse models. The technician is responsible for performing animal procedures, collecting biological samples, maintaining accurate animal and study records, and ensuring compliance with institutional IACUC protocols and animal welfare regulations. The technician will assist with the design and execution of preclinical studies. The position will interact with multiple investigators and work closely with other USC Norris core facilities.

The ideal candidate will have experience with oncology mouse models, strong technical skills in rodent procedures, excellent organizational abilities, and a commitment to generating high-quality preclinical data in a collaborative core facility environment.

**Essential job duties include, but are not limited to:**

* Independently perform preclinical in vivo research studies following approved protocols.

* Monitor and evaluate animal health, welfare, and protocol endpoints.

* Perform routine mouse procedures such as handling, restraint, identification, measurements, injections, blood collection, surgeries, imaging and euthanasia.

* Collect, process, and maintain biological specimens for downstream analyses.

* Maintain accurate experimental records and prepare study reports.

* Maintain laboratory equipment and inventory; order supplies as needed.

* Interact with investigators to assess research needs, coordinate services and communicate study progress.

* Assist in maintaining standard operating procedures and IACUC protocols.

* Prepare service quotes, generate invoices, and perform billing activities.

* Perform other related duties as needed.

  
  

**Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in Biology, Biomedical Sciences, or a related scientific discipline.
* Experience working with laboratory mice or other small laboratory animals.
* Demonstrated proficiency in small animal handling techniques and procedures.
  

  

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Minimum two years of laboratory animal research experience, including hands-on experience with laboratory mice.

* Proficiency in advanced mouse procedures such as tail vein injections and survival surgeries.

* Familiarity with preclinical models for oncology research.

* Experience working in an academic core facility, or academic research environment.

* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to work effectively with investigators and multidisciplinary teams.

  
  

Follows established USC and department policies, procedures, objectives, performance improvement, attendance, safety, environmental, and infection control guidelines, including adherence to the workplace Code of Conduct and Compliance Plan.

  
  

This position is on-site and employee must report to work at the USC Health Science Campus in Los Angeles, CA when scheduled. Work hours and on-site days may be subject to change depending on business needs.

  
  

The hourly rate range for this position is **$25.71 - $28.00**. When extending an offer of employment, the University of Southern California considers factors such as (but not limited to) the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate's work experience, education/training, key skills, internal peer equity, federal, state and local laws, contractual stipulations, grant funding, as well as external market and organizational considerations.

  
  
Minimum Education: Associate's degree, Specialized/technical training, Combined experience/education as substitute for minimum education Minimum Experience: 2 years Minimum Field of Expertise: Working knowledge of laboratory equipment and research protocols. Knowledge of computer analysis techniques and ability to provide routine analysis and interpretation of research data.

jobs.title: Laboratory Technician
jobs.description:
**Laboratory Technician**  
  
**Caltech**

**Job Category:** Fulltime Regular  
**Exempt Overtime Eligible:** Overtime Eligible  
**Benefits Eligible:** Benefit Based
  
  
Caltech is a world-renowned science and engineering institute that marshals some of the world's brightest minds and most innovative tools to address fundamental scientific questions. We thrive on finding and cultivating talented people who are passionate about what they do. Join us and be a part of the diverse Caltech community.  
  
**Job Summary**  
  
A Caltech Lab is seeking a Laboratory Technician to support the day-to-day technical operations of its cleanroom facilities on the Caltech campus.  
  
The Technician will help maintain and organize the cleanroom labs - wet/dry labs, mechanical equipment rooms, and supply and chemical storage areas - keeping supplies well stocked and daily operations running smoothly for the lab's research team, while working closely with senior technicians and equipment engineers.  
  
The Technician will assist with routine, hands-on tasks and gradually take on greater responsibility - including nanofabrication equipment maintenance and facilities coordination - as they build experience. Overall, the Technician is expected to contribute to the lab's culture and capabilities and grow into a more developed technician role over time.  
  
**Essential Job Duties**  
**Facilities monitoring and coordination:**  

* Monitor lab facility systems (HVAC, electrical, plumbing, compressed gas, and DI water lines) for signs of malfunction - unusual noise, temperature drift, leaks, alarms - and report issues promptly to the Lab Manager and/or Caltech Facilities.
* Track critical environmental parameters (temperature, humidity, particle counts, gas levels) that affect equipment performance and researcher safety, and escalate deviations quickly.

**Inventory and procurement:**  

* Organize and perform inventory counts of stockroom supplies, including equipment, maintenance spares, consumables, PPE, chemicals, gas cylinders, and other hazardous and nonhazardous materials.
* Place orders for consumables and coordinate delivery with vendors. Flag vendor issues (communication, quality, lead time) to the lab supervisor and help resolve them.

The Hoover Institution at Stanford University is seeking an **Audience & Marketing Insights Analyst** to join its Marketing and Communications team. The role is part marketing analyst, part analytics engineer: the analyst builds the pipelines and data models that connect Hoover’s platforms, then uses that data to answer four questions:

**What resonates?** Which content, campaigns, fellows, topics, and formats meaningfully connect with those audiences, and why?

**What deepens relationships?** Which actions and experiences move people from a single encounter with Hoover to repeat engagement, subscriptions, event attendance, and a lasting, direct relationship with the Institution?

**Job Summary**  
  
The Darkwah-Oppong Lab in the Division of Physics, Mathematics and Astronomy seeks a Research Assistant to join an experimental Atomic, Molecular, and Optical (AMO) physics laboratory focused on quantum science with neutral atoms. The group builds and operates optical tweezer arrays of individually trapped, laser-cooled neutral atoms to study quantum simulation, quantum metrology, and many-body physics. The successful candidate will contribute to the construction, operation, and improvement of an ultra-high-vacuum cold-atom apparatus, including laser and optical systems, high-resolution imaging, and the control and data-acquisition software used to prepare, manipulate, and measure atomic quantum states.
  
  
This is a hands-on, full-cycle research role intended to prepare the candidate for a PhD program in experimental quantum physics. The Research Assistant will work closely with the faculty sponsor, postdoctoral scholars, and graduate students, taking ownership of well-defined subprojects spanning hardware (lasers, optics, electronics, vacuum) and software (experimental control, simulation, and data analysis). The position offers broad training in the experimental and computational methods underlying modern quantum technologies.

* Develop, test, and document experimental control software, data-acquisition routines, and automated calibration sequences (primarily in Python).
* Perform numerical simulations and modeling of atomic and many-body systems to support experimental design and interpretation (e.g., lattice/tweezer trapping, single-particle and many-body dynamics).
* Collect, analyze, and visualize experimental data; apply statistical and computational methods to extract physical quantities and characterize system performance.
* Contribute to the design and fabrication of custom electronics, mechanical mounts, and printed-circuit boards as needed.
* Maintain detailed electronic lab notebooks and contribute to manuscripts, internal documentation, and group presentations.

* Bachelor's degree in Physics, Engineering Physics, or a closely related field by the position start date.
* Coursework in atomic, molecular, and optical physics and/or quantum mechanics.
* Demonstrated research experience in experimental and/or computational physics.
* Programming proficiency in Python (or equivalent) for simulation, data analysis, and instrument control.
* Strong quantitative, analytical, and problem-solving skills, with attention to detail and careful record-keeping.
* Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a team-based research environment. Ability to travel as needed for conferences and collaboration meetings.

  
**Preferred Qualifications**  

* Coursework or research experience in quantum simulation, quantum metrology, condensed matter, or many-body physics.
* Hands-on experience with laser-cooled atoms, optical lattices, ultracold atomic gases, or other AMO experimental platforms.
* Experience with optical alignment, lasers, vacuum systems, RF/microwave electronics, or FPGA-based control hardware.

The Innovative Genomics Institute (IGI) is a partnership between the University of California, Berkeley and the University of California, San Francisco. The Institutes mission is to accelerate genome discovery and translation of resulting technologies in order to ethically and equitably improve human health and sustainable agriculture. Combining fundamental research expertise and biomedical talent, the IGI focuses on unraveling the mechanisms underlying CRISPR-based genome editing and applying this technology to cure disease, combat climate change, ensure food sustainability, and provide additional benefits for current and future generations.
  
  
**The IGI consists of four central programs:** Human Health, Sustainable Agriculture, Advancing Genome Engineering, and Public Impact.
